Bitonality is the use of two keys at the same time in the same passage.
A suspension holds a note from one chord into the next, where it clashes before resolving down by step.
An appoggiatura is a non-chord note that delays a chord note, usually on a strong beat, and then resolves by step.
Modal mixture borrows notes or chords from the major or minor scale that shares a piece’s tonic.
A lament bass descends from the tonic to the dominant, often repeating beneath a song of grief.
Counterpoint combines melodic lines that keep their own shape and rhythm while sounding together.
Imitation occurs when one voice repeats a melody or fragment already stated by another voice.
A canon is a melody imitated by another voice at a fixed distance in time.
Homophony is a texture in which one part carries the melody and the other parts supply its harmony.
An ostinato is a short musical pattern repeated persistently while the music around it changes.
A motif is a short, recognisable musical idea that can be repeated, altered and combined with other ideas.
A leitmotif is a recurring musical idea associated with a character, object or thought in a drama.
Cyclic form links the movements of a work by bringing back themes heard in earlier movements.
Orchestration assigns music to instruments and combines their sounds.
Divisi tells the players in an instrumental section to divide between separate parts.
Pizzicato means plucking the strings of a bowed instrument with a finger.
